# Chain Council

![[_assets/banners/chain-council-banner.webp]]

*Closest thing to regional rule: loose, slow, wary, and strong when enough islands align.*

The [[midchain|Midchain]] governs loosely, stepping in only when a problem crosses island lines — every island stays sovereign, and the Council convenes at [[kalowe|Kalowe]], the largest port, where the best shipyard sits on the most neutral ground available. It moves slow and trusts no one, pushes back hard on any answer that costs an island its freedom, but strikes fast once enough islands share a threat. Its message to outsiders is blunt: name the risk, never absorb it — land on [[murrat|Murrat]] without invitation and the Council won't act, since Murrat keeps its own laws and enforcers; [[kalowe|Kalowe]] sits opposite, bending toward shared rule yet bristling at the Council's presence even while hosting it.

Council work spans reefs and routes, trade alerts, quarantine, lost ships, and cargo rights; it counters raids from the [[dravosi-crown|Dravosi Crown]] and [[tessarine-concordat|Tessarine Concordat]], and manages the border fighting near [[campaigns/shattered-sea/locations/verdant-teeth|Verdant Teeth]], hiring ships to raid when it needs force but never courting outright war. [[kalowe|Kalowe]]'s dry dock is the only fair shipyard in the Midchain — the Council owns it, sees every vessel that passes through, and can seize any ship it needs; port fees cover the costs, but the real power is knowing who is buying ships and where they're headed. [[campaigns/shattered-sea/vehicles/the-quorum|The Quorum]] is the Council's own patrol boat.

## Members

Harbourmasters, pilot elders, family heads, merchants, and shrine speakers — each island sends whoever it trusts most, and only the islands with a stake in a given matter shape the outcome. Others may speak or trade favors, but any decision that ignores those who pay the price collapses the moment they sail home. The source lists no formal membership roster; representation is ad hoc per matter, not a standing seat list.

## Goals & Fronts

Standing agenda: preserve island independence, coordinate on shared crises, and control [[kalowe|Kalowe]]'s dry dock as neutral shipyard.

An unknown backer had the Council gather a five-ship fleet under [[delmar-fisk|Admiral Delmar Fisk]] to claim the [[pearl-of-souls|Pearl of Souls]], an [[umberlee|Umberlee]] artifact in [[campaigns/shattered-sea/locations/sunken-crown/umberlee-shrine|the Blue Shrine]] at [[campaigns/shattered-sea/locations/sunken-crown/vel-orn|Vel Orn]] (see [[campaigns/shattered-sea/factions/fisks-fleet|Fisk's Fleet]]). [[campaigns/shattered-sea/npcs/cosimo-verantio|Cosimo Verantio]], a [[tessarine-concordat|Tessarine Concordat]] agent, hid behind a Council signatory's visible hand, posing as a backer known only as "the Principal"; the plan reached the Council via [[campaigns/shattered-sea/npcs/detto-kalash|Detto Kalash]]'s mail, and Kalash believed he carried nothing more than letters. The Council believed the deal would spare it from Umberlee's wrath — the real goal was halting [[campaigns/shattered-sea/npcs/aldric-drave|Aldric Drave]] from breaking his bloodline limits, and the Council never found out. In s04, [[delmar-fisk|Delmar Fisk]] confessed on the walk back to harbor that he commanded a real five-ship privateer fleet sponsored by the Chain Council, which stole the Pearl of Souls from a shrine at [[campaigns/shattered-sea/locations/sunken-crown|the Sunken Crown]] before the Maw destroyed the fleet (`vault/episodes/004/transcript.md:30`).

The [[campaigns/shattered-sea/factions/fisks-fleet|Fisk's Fleet]] commission (destroyed by the Maw in s04) is the live threat, and its political fallout shapes four Fronts below.

### Front: Denial

**Lifecycle:** active. **Trigger conditions:** evidence of the Council's role in the Pearl of Souls commission surfaces but is not made public.

**Primary goal:** keep the Council's sponsorship of the commission unconfirmed, so no single signatory answers for it alone. **Consistent method:** agrees a closed-session line before facing inquiry, then routes every direct question back to procedure. **Off-screen move if unopposed:** quietly reroutes or destroys [[campaigns/shattered-sea/npcs/detto-kalash|Detto Kalash]]'s mail record, so "the Principal"'s letters dead-end at a lost ledger.

**Clock:** 4 segments (fast-moving), filled: 0. **Consequence at fill:** representatives privately blame each other. The official record hardens around "bad intelligence."

**Possible outcomes (2-3):** [[uncertainty|the Uncertainty]]'s crew surfaces hard evidence before the fill, splitting the Council and forcing a signatory to answer publicly. If they help bury it instead, the Council owes them quietly. Left alone, the consequence fires as written, and Delmar's name enters the "bad intelligence" story as the convenient admiral to blame.

**PC connection:** [[delmar-fisk|Delmar Fisk]]. Real, findable admiral. Easiest scapegoat when the Council needs a name.

### Front: Tessarine Containment

**Lifecycle:** active. **Trigger conditions:** a Tessarine agent learns someone has evidence.

**Primary goal:** keep [[campaigns/shattered-sea/npcs/cosimo-verantio|Cosimo Verantio]]'s "Principal" cover intact, so the Concordat's real hand in the commission, and its true target [[campaigns/shattered-sea/npcs/aldric-drave|Aldric Drave]], never surfaces. **Consistent method:** calls in standing credit and debt holds on Council-adjacent signatories to buy silence before ever making a direct threat.

**Off-screen move if unopposed:** a factor quietly buys out or re-terms whoever starts asking questions near [[campaigns/shattered-sea/npcs/detto-kalash|Detto Kalash]]'s mail route, closing the trail with money before it needs force.

**Clock:** 6 segments (slow burn), filled: 0. **Consequence at fill:** political pressure spreads island by island before the next Council meeting through both inducements (protection, debt relief) and threats.

**Possible outcomes (2-3):** the crew reaches Cosimo before containment completes, exposing the Concordat's real hand and Aldric Drave as the true target. Left alone, pressure spreads island by island as stated, and the Council never learns who was truly behind it. Or a pressured signatory takes the Tessarine deal, handing the Concordat a new obligated vote the Chain never sees coming.

**PC connection:** [[campaigns/shattered-sea/pcs/perrin-black-jaw|Perrin Black-Jaw]]. Tessarine pressure squeezes his community without anyone naming him.

### Front: Midchain Anger

**Lifecycle:** active. **Trigger conditions:** coastal settlements hear the Council spent money on the Pearl while [[grung|Grung]] raids worsened.

**Primary goal:** keep coastal anger over the Pearl spending as grumbling, not a legitimacy challenge against [[kalowe|Kalowe]] and the Chain. **Consistent method:** counters rising anger by sending patrols or grain shipments to whichever island protests loudest that week.

**Off-screen move if unopposed:** diverts [[campaigns/shattered-sea/vehicles/the-quorum|The Quorum]] from reef patrol to a raided coastal settlement, buying goodwill there while another goes unanswered.

**Clock:** 4 segments (fast-moving), filled: 0. **Consequence at fill:** the [[campaigns/shattered-sea/locations/verdant-teeth|Verdant Teeth]] crisis becomes a legitimacy crisis for [[kalowe|Kalowe]] and the Chain.

**Possible outcomes (2-3):** if the Uncertainty's crew helps a raided settlement directly, they buy the Council time it hasn't earned. Left alone, the consequence fires as written. If they publicize the Pearl spending instead, the Council's relief strategy collapses overnight.

**PC connection:** [[jean-claude-tabarnack|Jean-Claude Tabarnack]]. Fled the [[campaigns/shattered-sea/locations/verdant-teeth|Verdant Teeth]]; his sister [[simone-tabarnack|Simone]] leads their raiders, narrowing his path home.

### Front: Umberlee's Accounting

**Lifecycle:** active. **Trigger conditions:** the Council's role reaches a Waveservant Shrine.

**Primary goal:** keep the Council's role in the theft from ever reaching a [[waveservants|Waveservant]] shrine, since a Waveservant hearing it makes the debt divine, not political. **Consistent method:** keeps its shrine dealings transactional and unremarkable, paying ordinary tribute and volunteering nothing beyond what's asked.

**Off-screen move if unopposed:** quietly raises tribute at the [[kalowe|Kalowe]] shrine well above the going rate, hoping goodwill buys silence if a Waveservant ever starts listening too closely.

**Clock:** 6 segments (slow burn), filled: 0. **Consequence at fill:** the Council becomes part of the divine debt, regardless of intent.

**Possible outcomes (2-3):** the Uncertainty's crew keeps the Council's role from any shrine, and the consequence never fires. It reaches a shrine anyway, and the Council becomes part of the divine debt as stated. Or a signatory confesses to a Waveservant privately to buy personal absolution, splitting the Council's exposure from its own cover story.

**PC connection:** [[crissdalynn-khinriss|Crissdalynn Khinriss]]. Fleet survivor who pulled Fisk from the wreck. Shrine scrutiny reaches her with him.
